feedback.problem:
The velocity $v$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
v=⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{t+1}},\,-1⟩,\,t\ge 0.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $(5,2)$ when $t=3,$ calculate the position vector of $P$ at time $t.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{t+1}},\,-1⟩\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{t+1}}\,\text{d}t,\,\int (-1)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨2\sqrt{t+1}+{C}_{1},\,-t+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(3)=⟨5,2⟩.$ Substituting $t=3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(3) & =⟨2\sqrt{3+1}+{C}_{1},\,-3+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨5,2⟩ & =⟨4+{C}_{1},-3+{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=1$ and ${C}_{2}=5.$ Therefore, the position vector is

$$
r(t)=⟨2\sqrt{t+1}+1,\,5-t⟩.
$$
